jobs.description:
Company Description
Water, Inc. is a leading provider of high-quality drinking water systems and the premier representative for these solutions across the Western United States. We offer eco-friendly, advanced water filtration systems that help reduce plastic waste while delivering safe, filtered water. Water, Inc. provides a comprehensive range of products that filter, heat, brew, chill, soften, and dispense water for residential and commercial customers. The organization is supported by knowledgeable sales professionals and specialized programs. Applicants can expect to join a company focused on sustainability, innovation, and customer service.

Role Description
The Business Operations Manager (Order Flow, Purchasing & Systems) is a full-time, on-site role based in Los Angeles, CA. This role oversees end-to-end order flow, ensuring accurate and timely processing from order entry through fulfillment and post-sales support. The manager coordinates purchasing activities, manages vendor relationships, and monitors inventory levels to maintain optimal stock and cost efficiency. Day-to-day responsibilities include analyzing operational data, improving processes, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to enhance system performance and business workflows. The role also involves managing operational programs, supporting budgeting and cost control efforts, and implementing systems and tools that improve visibility, efficiency, and customer experience.
Qualifications

Demonstrated expertise in Business Operations and Operations Management to oversee order flow, purchasing, and system processes.
Strong Analytical Skills to interpret data, identify trends, and recommend process improvements.
Experience in Program Management to coordinate operational initiatives and cross-functional projects.
Working knowledge of Finance to support budgeting, cost analysis, and vendor pricing evaluations.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proficiency with ERP or order management systems, and strong Excel or data analysis skills.
Excellent organizational, communication, and stakeholder management abilities, with attention to detail and follow-through.
Experience in consumer products, water treatment, or related industries is beneficial, as is familiarity with inventory and logistics best practices.

The Role Orders come in, primarily through B2B customers. Product gets bought, stocked, picked, and shipped. Customers call when something isn't right. You're the person who owns the space between them, and you're the person who makes sure things run properly.

You'll sit between the order desk and the warehouse, handle our purchasing, and make sure work actually gets finished. Not by watching a dashboard. By knowing how an order should move through this company, noticing when it doesn't, and fixing the thing that caused it.

You'll also be our internal owner of the ERP system. You'll report to the President and work with him directly. There's a lot of room here to change how a 49-year-old company operates.

What You'll Own Order flow, end to end.
Every order that comes in, from entry through purchase, allocation, shipment, and invoice. You own the accuracy and the turnaround. When an order stalls, you're the one who knows where it is and why. We have a great warehouse manager, and you won't be on the floor.

The ERP system.
You'll be the internal expert: order entry, inventory, pricing, purchasing, customer and vendor records, reports. Understanding how it's set up, where it's set up wrong, and how to fix that. We run Prophet21. We're also bringing in new tools, including AI-assisted document processing that reads incoming POs and quotes, and we want someone who's interested in using that well rather than nervous about it.

Purchasing.
You will help manage and execute what we buy and when. Reorder points, lead times, vendor relationships, expediting when a customer order depends on it. You'll help create a process for this as a function of this job.

Inventory.
Keeping item and pricing data clean, running and reconciling counts, and staying ahead of stockouts on the products that matter instead of reacting to them. You will occasionally run inventory audits.

Clean data for our accounting firm.
Our accounting is handled by an outside firm. You are not doing the books, the close, or the reconciliations. You are the person who makes sure what they’re closing is real, that data entered into P21 from orders is correct: POs received correctly, invoices matched, inventory transactions posted right, vendor and customer records accurate. When they ask why a number moved, you’re who they call. You also will run and maintain Crystal Reports.

Customer service, and customer escalations.
First, ensuring that we are providing great service to our customers. And when necessary, fielding the hard calls, the disputed orders, the mistakes we made. You're the escalation point, and you close the loop on the underlying cause.

Process.
Writing the SOPs that don't exist, fixing the ones that don't work, and making sure people follow them.

Who You Are You've spent your career at a company that makes or sells physical products, and you've been the person people come to when something is stuck. You're organized without being rigid, you follow up without being asked, and you're comfortable telling someone their part of the process is the problem.

You're hands-on. This is a small company. Some days you'll be solving a systems problem, and some days you'll be entering an order because it has to go out today. Neither is beneath the job.

What We're Looking For -      5 to 10 years in operations, purchasing, order management, or business systems at a distribution, wholesale, or manufacturing company
-      Real buying experience: POs, vendors, lead times, reorder decisions, and the judgment to know when to hold inventory and when not to
-      Real ownership of daily order flow: entry, fulfillment, exceptions, and the customers on the other end of them
-      Hands-on depth in an ERP system. We use Prophet21, but if you have gone in depth with another advanced ERP system (SAP, NetSuite, Dynamics, Sage, Acumatica, Epicor, etc) and understand how it's configured and why things break, you'll learn P21. Running standard reports and opening tickets is not the same thing.
-      Enough financial fluency to know what a clean transaction looks like and why it matters downstream
-      Comfortable coordinating across people you don't necessarily manage
-      Clear, direct communicator, in writing and on the phone
-      On-site in Carson, five days a week

Nice to have, not required: supervisory experience, Shopify or another e-commerce platform, Crystal Reports or SQL, experience through an ERP implementation or conversion.

What This Is Not This is not a warehouse role. You're not running a crew or driving a forklift or packing orders, but you will help liaise with them and our sales team and dealers to make sure things run smoothly.

We're looking for someone who will own the operational middle of this company and make it run cleanly, every day. And while it's not an accounting job, some of the responsibilities will help support our outside accounting firm, but you won't be closing the books.

Details $90,000 to $105,000, depending on experience. Health, dental, vision. 401(k) with company match. Paid time off. Full-time, on-site, Carson CA.

To apply:
tell us briefly about an operational problem you found that nobody had asked you to look at, and what you changed. Cover letters are read.

No recruiters, please.

About the Role

We are looking for a high-potential Product Information Management (PIM) & AI Data Analyst to help build a scalable, high-quality product data capability for a large distribution business. The role sits at the intersection of product information, data analysis, process design and AI-enabled research.
This is not a data-entry or traditional catalogue administration role. The successful candidate will work with large and imperfect datasets, determine how information should be structured and standardized, identify patterns and exceptions, and build repeatable rules that improve the quality and scalability of product information.

Prior automotive or industry-specific product knowledge is not required. The domain can be taught. We are primarily looking for someone who can think analytically, learn quickly, work confidently with data, and use modern AI applications as part of their day-to-day problem solving.

What You Will Do
Structure, clean, standardize and enrich product information received from multiple internal and external sources.
Help build and maintain product hierarchies, categories, attributes, naming conventions and data-quality rules.
Compare datasets from different suppliers or systems and determine where records are equivalent, inconsistent, incomplete or require further investigation.
Translate unstructured or inconsistent product information into structured, PIM-ready datasets.
Develop repeatable rules for classification, matching, enrichment and validation rather than relying on one-off manual fixes.
Create exception-based workflows so human effort is focused on ambiguous or high-value records instead of reviewing every record manually.
Work with Product, Commercial, E-commerce and Data teams to understand how product information is used and what data quality is required.
Document logic, business rules and data standards clearly so that they can be reused and scaled.

AI-Enabled Research & Analysis

A central part of this role is the practical use of modern AI tools. We are looking for someone who is already comfortable experimenting with AI, or has the aptitude to become a highly effective AI user quickly.

Use applications such as ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini or similar tools to accelerate research and analysis.
Use AI to interpret unstructured descriptions, technical documents, spreadsheets and other product information.
Design and refine prompts that help classify records, compare information, identify patterns, suggest rules and surface anomalies.
Use AI to assist with Excel formulas, SQL queries, Python scripts or data-transformation logic where appropriate.
Develop AI-assisted workflows that reduce repetitive manual research and improve processing speed.
Critically validate AI-generated outputs against reliable sources and underlying data before they are accepted.
Identify where AI can automate a task, where deterministic rules are more appropriate, and where human judgement is still required.

Data Analysis & Problem Solving

Work comfortably with datasets containing thousands to hundreds of thousands of records.
Use Excel to filter, compare, reconcile, transform and analyse large product datasets.
Identify duplicates, near-duplicates, missing attributes, inconsistent terminology and data-quality issues.
Analyse how information from different sources maps to a common structure.
Create simple metrics and exception reports to measure completeness, consistency and data quality.
Break ambiguous problems into clear decision rules and test those rules across larger datasets.
Investigate unexpected results rather than simply processing records as provided.

PIM, Taxonomy & Product Data

Support the design and maintenance of product category hierarchies and taxonomies.
Define which attributes are required for different categories and how those attributes should be represented.
Help determine which data should be mandatory, optional, customer-facing, searchable or used internally.
Create consistent product naming and description standards.
Support data migration, supplier onboarding and product-data enrichment activities.
Help ensure that product data is usable across PIM, e-commerce, analytics and commercial applications.

Strong analytical and structured problem-solving
Advanced Excel skills or the ability to reach that level quickly
PIM, master data, catalogue or product-data
Experience with taxonomy, classification or data
SQL, Python, Power Query or similar data ability
Comfort working with large and imperfect datasets tooling
Strong attention to detail and an instinct for finding inconsistencies
Comfort using modern generative-AI applications
Ability to learn unfamiliar domains quickly
Experience with e-commerce or supplier datasets

BONUS: Automotive or distribution-industry knowledge
BONUS: Experience designing AI-assisted data workflows

Independently take ownership of datasets or product categories after an initial learning period.
Turn messy source information into reliable, structured and usable product data.
Build rules and workflows that materially reduce manual effort.
Use AI as a genuine productivity and research tool while maintaining strong validation standards.
Communicate clearly with both business and technical stakeholders.
Create documentation that allows processes and decisions to be repeated consistently.
Help move the product-data operating model toward a more data-driven, rules-based and AI-enabled way of working.

This is an opportunity to work on a practical product-data transformation rather than simply administer an existing system. Boys Club is a culture-forward media brand and creative studio operating within Polygon Labs, at the intersection of tech, finance, and internet culture. The briefing workflows, trafficking processes, approval chains, and production infrastructure you build here will be the systems the team runs on going forward. If you are someone who needs a well-defined system before you can perform, you will find this environment genuinely difficult. However, if you're energised by building systems and turning chaos into order, you should keep reading!

You will be the operational centre of Boys Club: the person who holds every active deliverable across paid client work and editorial content in their head and on the board, keeps the team unblocked, and makes sure nothing ships late, off brief, or over budget. You report to the Head of Strategy and Partnerships, and you sit at the execution layer of almost every project this team touches.

Own the content calendar, pipeline, status tracking, and production processes across both paid client deliverables and Boys Club editorial content (Malware, Too Online, Boys Club Live), so every asset in production has a clear owner, a due date, and a documented next step at all times

Company Description
Water, Inc. is a leading provider of high-quality drinking water systems and the premier representative for these solutions across the Western United States. Water, Inc. provides a comprehensive range of products that filter, heat, brew, chill, soften, and dispense water for residential and commercial customers. The organization is supported by knowledgeable sales professionals and specialized programs. Applicants can expect to join a company focused on sustainability, innovation, and customer service.

Role Description
The Business Operations Manager (Order Flow, Purchasing & Systems) is a full-time, on-site role based in Los Angeles, CA. This role oversees end-to-end order flow, ensuring accurate and timely processing from order entry through fulfillment and post-sales support. The manager coordinates purchasing activities, manages vendor relationships, and monitors inventory levels to maintain optimal stock and cost efficiency. Day-to-day responsibilities include analyzing operational data, improving processes, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to enhance system performance and business workflows. The role also involves managing operational programs, supporting budgeting and cost control efforts, and implementing systems and tools that improve visibility, efficiency, and customer experience.
Qualifications

Demonstrated expertise in Business Operations and Operations Management to oversee order flow, purchasing, and system processes.
Strong Analytical Skills to interpret data, identify trends, and recommend process improvements.
Experience in Program Management to coordinate operational initiatives and cross-functional projects.
Working knowledge of Finance to support budgeting, cost analysis, and vendor pricing evaluations.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Operations Management, Supply Chain, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proficiency with ERP or order management systems, and strong Excel or data analysis skills.
Excellent organizational, communication, and stakeholder management abilities, with attention to detail and follow-through.
Experience in consumer products, water treatment, or related industries is beneficial, as is familiarity with inventory and logistics best practices.

The Role Orders come in, primarily through B2B customers. Product gets bought, stocked, picked, and shipped. Customers call when something isn't right. You're the person who owns the space between them, and you're the person who makes sure things run properly.

You'll sit between the order desk and the warehouse, handle our purchasing, and make sure work actually gets finished. Not by watching a dashboard. By knowing how an order should move through this company, noticing when it doesn't, and fixing the thing that caused it.

You'll also be our internal owner of the ERP system. You'll report to the President and work with him directly. There's a lot of room here to change how a 49-year-old company operates.

What You'll Own Order flow, end to end.
Every order that comes in, from entry through purchase, allocation, shipment, and invoice. You own the accuracy and the turnaround. When an order stalls, you're the one who knows where it is and why. We have a great warehouse manager, and you won't be on the floor.

The ERP system.
You'll be the internal expert: order entry, inventory, pricing, purchasing, customer and vendor records, reports. Understanding how it's set up, where it's set up wrong, and how to fix that. We run Prophet21. We're also bringing in new tools, including AI-assisted document processing that reads incoming POs and quotes, and we want someone who's interested in using that well rather than nervous about it.

Purchasing.
You will help manage and execute what we buy and when. Reorder points, lead times, vendor relationships, expediting when a customer order depends on it. You'll help create a process for this as a function of this job.

Inventory.
Keeping item and pricing data clean, running and reconciling counts, and staying ahead of stockouts on the products that matter instead of reacting to them. You will occasionally run inventory audits.

Clean data for our accounting firm.
Our accounting is handled by an outside firm. You are not doing the books, the close, or the reconciliations. You are the person who makes sure what they’re closing is real, that data entered into P21 from orders is correct: POs received correctly, invoices matched, inventory transactions posted right, vendor and customer records accurate. When they ask why a number moved, you’re who they call. You also will run and maintain Crystal Reports.

Customer service, and customer escalations.
First, ensuring that we are providing great service to our customers. And when necessary, fielding the hard calls, the disputed orders, the mistakes we made. You're the escalation point, and you close the loop on the underlying cause.

Process.
Writing the SOPs that don't exist, fixing the ones that don't work, and making sure people follow them.

Who You Are You've spent your career at a company that makes or sells physical products, and you've been the person people come to when something is stuck. You're organized without being rigid, you follow up without being asked, and you're comfortable telling someone their part of the process is the problem.

You're hands-on. This is a small company. Some days you'll be solving a systems problem, and some days you'll be entering an order because it has to go out today. Neither is beneath the job.

What We're Looking For -      5 to 10 years in operations, purchasing, order management, or business systems at a distribution, wholesale, or manufacturing company
-      Real buying experience: POs, vendors, lead times, reorder decisions, and the judgment to know when to hold inventory and when not to
-      Real ownership of daily order flow: entry, fulfillment, exceptions, and the customers on the other end of them
-      Hands-on depth in an ERP system. We use Prophet21, but if you have gone in depth with another advanced ERP system (SAP, NetSuite, Dynamics, Sage, Acumatica, Epicor, etc) and understand how it's configured and why things break, you'll learn P21. Running standard reports and opening tickets is not the same thing.
-      Enough financial fluency to know what a clean transaction looks like and why it matters downstream
-      Comfortable coordinating across people you don't necessarily manage
-      Clear, direct communicator, in writing and on the phone
-      On-site in Carson, five days a week

Nice to have, not required: supervisory experience, Shopify or another e-commerce platform, Crystal Reports or SQL, experience through an ERP implementation or conversion.

What This Is Not This is not a warehouse role. You're not running a crew or driving a forklift or packing orders, but you will help liaise with them and our sales team and dealers to make sure things run smoothly.

We're looking for someone who will own the operational middle of this company and make it run cleanly, every day. And while it's not an accounting job, some of the responsibilities will help support our outside accounting firm, but you won't be closing the books.

Details $90,000 to $105,000, depending on experience. Health, dental, vision. 401(k) with company match. Paid time off. Full-time, on-site, Carson CA.

To apply:
tell us briefly about an operational problem you found that nobody had asked you to look at, and what you changed. Cover letters are read.

No recruiters, please.

About the Role

We are looking for a high-potential Product Information Management (PIM) & AI Data Analyst to help build a scalable, high-quality product data capability for a large distribution business. The role sits at the intersection of product information, data analysis, process design and AI-enabled research.
This is not a data-entry or traditional catalogue administration role. The successful candidate will work with large and imperfect datasets, determine how information should be structured and standardized, identify patterns and exceptions, and build repeatable rules that improve the quality and scalability of product information.

Prior automotive or industry-specific product knowledge is not required. The domain can be taught. We are primarily looking for someone who can think analytically, learn quickly, work confidently with data, and use modern AI applications as part of their day-to-day problem solving.

What You Will Do
Structure, clean, standardize and enrich product information received from multiple internal and external sources.
Help build and maintain product hierarchies, categories, attributes, naming conventions and data-quality rules.
Compare datasets from different suppliers or systems and determine where records are equivalent, inconsistent, incomplete or require further investigation.
Translate unstructured or inconsistent product information into structured, PIM-ready datasets.
Develop repeatable rules for classification, matching, enrichment and validation rather than relying on one-off manual fixes.
Create exception-based workflows so human effort is focused on ambiguous or high-value records instead of reviewing every record manually.
Work with Product, Commercial, E-commerce and Data teams to understand how product information is used and what data quality is required.
Document logic, business rules and data standards clearly so that they can be reused and scaled.

AI-Enabled Research & Analysis

A central part of this role is the practical use of modern AI tools. We are looking for someone who is already comfortable experimenting with AI, or has the aptitude to become a highly effective AI user quickly.

Use applications such as ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini or similar tools to accelerate research and analysis.
Use AI to interpret unstructured descriptions, technical documents, spreadsheets and other product information.
Design and refine prompts that help classify records, compare information, identify patterns, suggest rules and surface anomalies.
Use AI to assist with Excel formulas, SQL queries, Python scripts or data-transformation logic where appropriate.
Develop AI-assisted workflows that reduce repetitive manual research and improve processing speed.
Critically validate AI-generated outputs against reliable sources and underlying data before they are accepted.
Identify where AI can automate a task, where deterministic rules are more appropriate, and where human judgement is still required.

Data Analysis & Problem Solving

Work comfortably with datasets containing thousands to hundreds of thousands of records.
Use Excel to filter, compare, reconcile, transform and analyse large product datasets.
Identify duplicates, near-duplicates, missing attributes, inconsistent terminology and data-quality issues.
Analyse how information from different sources maps to a common structure.
Create simple metrics and exception reports to measure completeness, consistency and data quality.
Break ambiguous problems into clear decision rules and test those rules across larger datasets.
Investigate unexpected results rather than simply processing records as provided.

PIM, Taxonomy & Product Data

Support the design and maintenance of product category hierarchies and taxonomies.
Define which attributes are required for different categories and how those attributes should be represented.
Help determine which data should be mandatory, optional, customer-facing, searchable or used internally.
Create consistent product naming and description standards.
Support data migration, supplier onboarding and product-data enrichment activities.
Help ensure that product data is usable across PIM, e-commerce, analytics and commercial applications.

Skills We Are Looking For

Strong analytical and structured problem-solving
Advanced Excel skills or the ability to reach that level quickly
PIM, master data, catalogue or product-data
Experience with taxonomy, classification or data
SQL, Python, Power Query or similar data ability
Comfort working with large and imperfect datasets tooling
Strong attention to detail and an instinct for finding inconsistencies
Comfort using modern generative-AI applications
Ability to learn unfamiliar domains quickly
Experience with e-commerce or supplier datasets

BONUS: Automotive or distribution-industry knowledge
BONUS: Experience designing AI-assisted data workflows

The Profile That Will Succeed

intensive environment.

The mindset we value is: understand the problem -> identify the underlying rule -> test it on the data -> automate what can be automated -> isolate exceptions -> document the logic.

Independently take ownership of datasets or product categories after an initial learning period.
Turn messy source information into reliable, structured and usable product data.
Build rules and workflows that materially reduce manual effort.
Use AI as a genuine productivity and research tool while maintaining strong validation standards.

Create documentation that allows processes and decisions to be repeated consistently.
Help move the product-data operating model toward a more data-driven, rules-based and AI-enabled way of working.

new_jobs.description:
About Polygon Labs

Polygon Labs is a global blockchain payments company building and operating infrastructure to move money instantly, reliably, and at internet scale, with the mission to move all money onchain. It is building the Polygon Open Money Stack, an open and integrated stack of services and technologies to instantly and reliably move money anywhere, and put it to work. Its infrastructure has facilitated trillions of dollars in onchain value transfer and supported millions of transactions daily for some of the globe's largest banks, fintechs, enterprises, and consumer applications.

Your Role

Boys Club is a culture-forward media brand and creative studio operating within Polygon Labs, at the intersection of tech, finance, and internet culture. The team runs paid client work and owned editorial properties simultaneously, and does both at a high standard. This role exists because that operation has grown to a scale where someone needs to own the entire production layer full-time.

This is a founding operations hire. There is no existing playbook. The briefing workflows, trafficking processes, approval chains, and production infrastructure you build here will be the systems the team runs on going forward. If you are someone who needs a well-defined system before you can perform, you will find this environment genuinely difficult. However, if you're energised by building systems and turning chaos into order, you should keep reading!

You will be the operational centre of Boys Club: the person who holds every active deliverable across paid client work and editorial content in their head and on the board, keeps the team unblocked, and makes sure nothing ships late, off brief, or over budget. You report to the Head of Strategy and Partnerships, and you sit at the execution layer of almost every project this team touches.

Contract structure: This is fixed-term contract position

Your Responsibilities

Own the content calendar, pipeline, status tracking, and production processes across both paid client deliverables and Boys Club editorial content (Malware, Too Online, Boys Club Live), so every asset in production has a clear owner, a due date, and a documented next step at all times
Build and implement the briefing, trafficking, and approval workflows that the team runs on, from initial brief through internal review to final client delivery, so nothing goes live without sign-off and no one has to ask what the status of a deliverable is
Coordinate internal team members, external creative partners, and freelancers across multiple simultaneous projects: gather estimates, manage budget tracking alongside the Account Director, raise purchase orders, and keep every resource on track without requiring the Account Director to babysit individual engagements
Run weekly cross-functional standups with internal and external stakeholders: prepare agendas, facilitate the session, capture client feedback accurately, and convert meeting notes into tracked action items before the next session starts
Escalate scope changes, budget risks, and timeline slippage to the Account Director before they become real problems; your job is to surface risk early, not report it after it lands
Support the editorial and show production tracks with the same rigour as paid client work, managing the Boys Club Live production calendar, newsletter scheduling, and promotional asset timelines so neither track uses the other as an excuse to slip
Maintain current knowledge of platform algorithm updates and hook-testing approaches across short and long-form content formats, and apply that knowledge when reviewing social deliverables moving through the production pipeline
Use AI tools to accelerate the operational groundwork of the role: generating first-pass briefs, structuring standup agendas, organising client feedback into clean action item lists, and researching incoming partners; the expectation is that AI handles the scaffolding so your judgment goes into the decisions, not the formatting

What You'll Need

A track record of managing 20 or more creative assets simultaneously across multiple clients, formats, or content tracks, with evidence that you built or significantly improved the production infrastructure that made that volume manageable, not just that you survived it
Experience coordinating across creative teams, external clients or partners, and freelancers or agencies on the same projects simultaneously, with real accountability to all three at once; PM experience that is purely internal or purely client-facing will show a gap here
Strong written communication: crisp standup agendas, well-structured client recaps, and asset trafficking instructions that create clarity rather than more questions; in an async-heavy operation, unclear written communication creates downstream problems on every project you touch
Enough internet and cultural literacy to be a credible partner to a creative team with high standards; you do not need to be a content strategist, but you need to understand why a piece of work is or is not right for a specific audience, and why a late-to-the-moment deliverable is worse than one that does not ship at all
Demonstrated AI fluency as a daily operational practice: you use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Notion AI, or comparable) to handle structural and research tasks, freeing your attention for judgment calls; you can describe specifically where AI sits in your workflow and where it does not, and your final outputs reflect your own thinking, not unreviewed AI output

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience in a media, creator economy, or newsletter environment, with direct familiarity with how editorial and sponsored content tracks operate alongside each other
Experience managing paid content or sponsorship deliverables alongside owned editorial content in the same production operation, with direct accountability to external clients on deliverable timelines
A configured project management setup you can walk through in an interview: not the default out-of-the-box tool, but a system you have built, refined, and can explain, including where it has broken and what you changed
